reforms.description: Japan introduced R&D tax incentives for firms in FY2003, providing tax relief for research and development expenditures. The initial three-year temporary measures were largely terminated in FY2006, but the R&D incentive for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) was extended for another two years.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax incentives reduce the effective cost of innovation investment for firms, encouraging private-sector R&D spending and technological development that can raise productivity and long-term growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states: 'the corporate tax base was narrowed by the introduction of R&D and investment incentives in FY2003 for three years' and 'the R&D incentive for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) was extended for another two years' after FY2006.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant but targeted innovation instrument affecting private-sector R&D investment, particularly for SMEs. The extension beyond the initial three-year period indicates sustained policy commitment, though the scope is narrower than a system-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: the corporate tax base was narrowed by the introduction of R&D and investment incentives in FY2003 for three years, which resulted in an estimated 1.1 trillion yen (0.2% of GDP) of foregone tax revenue per year. Although the temporary measures were largely terminated in FY2006 as scheduled, the R&D incentive for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) was extended for another two years.

reforms.description: Japan introduced a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure, implemented alongside the extension of the R&D incentive for SMEs after FY2006. This measure aimed to support private-sector investment in digital and information technology infrastructure.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax incentives for information infrastructure investment reduce the cost of digital technology adoption, supporting private-sector innovation and productivity improvements in the digital economy.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states: 'new measures, including a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure, were introduced' after FY2006 when the R&D incentive for SMEs was extended.
reforms.importance_rationale: A minor, narrowly targeted tax incentive for information infrastructure acquisition. While supporting digital innovation, it is a temporary measure with limited scope compared to broader innovation policy instruments.
reforms.source_quote: new measures, including a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure, were introduced.

reforms.description: Japan implemented a tax subsidy for R&D designed to incentivize private-sector research and development spending. A permanent 10% increase in the tax subsidy was estimated to raise R&D spending by over 8%.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax subsidies reduce the cost of innovation for firms, incentivizing private investment in research and development, which raises productivity and long-run output per capita.
reforms.status_evidence: The text references the tax subsidy and its estimated effects but does not explicitly state the implementation, legislation, or announcement date.
reforms.importance_rationale: The R&D tax subsidy is a significant innovation instrument with measurable effects on private R&D spending (8% increase per 10% subsidy increase), but the text provides limited detail on scope, duration, or systemic impact.
reforms.source_quote: A permanent 10% increase in the tax subsidy for R&D was estimated to raise the level of R&D spending by over 8% (Jaumotte and Pain, 2005).

reforms.description: MEXT launched a project in FY2006 and FY2007 to promote diversification of career paths for researchers at public research institutes, enhancing labour mobility in the research sector.
reforms.package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing labour mobility and career flexibility for researchers increases human capital allocation efficiency and supports innovation capacity in the public research sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The MEXT launched a project to promote the diversification of the career path for researchers in FY2006 and FY2007.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted initiative to improve researcher mobility and career flexibility within public research institutes, supporting the broader goal of enhancing innovation capacity. Significant but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: The MEXT launched a project to promote the diversification of the career path for researchers in FY2006 and FY2007.

reforms.description: Following the 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006), research institutes and universities were directed to increase the number of researchers with fixed-term contracts to enhance labour mobility and reduce in-breeding.
reforms.package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing fixed-term contracts and reducing in-breeding enhances labour mobility, competitive hiring, and performance-based incentives in public research institutions, supporting innovation productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: Following the 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006), research institutes and universities are to increase the number of researchers with fixed-term contracts.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant structural reform of employment practices in public research institutions aimed at improving labour mobility and reducing institutional in-breeding. Affects hiring and career progression across the public research sector.
reforms.source_quote: Following the 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006), research institutes and universities are to increase the number of researchers with fixed-term contracts.

reforms.description: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006) promoted cooperation between business and R&D organisations through conferences to strengthen links between public research institutes and the business sector.
reforms.package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening links between public research and business sectors facilitates knowledge transfer and commercialisation, supporting innovation diffusion and private-sector productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology promotes co-operation between business and R&D organisations through conferences.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted initiative to improve university-industry collaboration through structured engagement mechanisms. Significant for knowledge transfer but relatively modest in scope and implementation mechanism.
reforms.source_quote: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology promotes co-operation between business and R&D organisations through conferences.

reforms.description: The share of competitive grants in central government R&D funding was increased from 12.6% in FY2006 to 13.6% in FY2007, with the amount rising from 471 billion yen to 477 billion yen.
reforms.package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing the share of competitive grants improves allocative efficiency in public R&D funding by directing resources to higher-quality research proposals and reducing institutional inertia.
reforms.status_evidence: The amount of competitive grants rose from 471 billion yen in FY2006 to 477 billion yen in FY2007, boosting its share in central government outlays on science and technology from 12.6% to 13.6%.
reforms.importance_rationale: An incremental but meaningful increase in competitive grant funding as a share of total R&D appropriations. Supports the broader policy goal of improving research quality and efficiency through merit-based allocation.
reforms.source_quote: The amount of competitive grants rose from 471 billion yen in FY2006 to 477 billion yen in FY2007, boosting its share in central government outlays on science and technology from 12.6% to 13.6%.

reforms.description: An action plan to reform the patent evaluation system was updated in January 2007 to improve the efficiency and framework of patent evaluation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving patent evaluation efficiency reduces transaction costs for innovators and strengthens intellectual property protection, supporting commercialisation of research and innovation incentives.
reforms.status_evidence: An action plan to reform the patent evaluation system was updated in January 2007.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted reform of the patent system to improve evaluation efficiency and reduce barriers to IP commercialisation. Significant for innovation incentives but narrower in scope than broader IP regime changes.
reforms.source_quote: An action plan to reform the patent evaluation system was updated in January 2007.

reforms.description: Disclosure by firms was improved to encourage investment by individual investors in venture businesses, supporting the development of venture capital markets while moving away from public debt guarantees.
reforms.component_name: Firm disclosure improvement for venture investment
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving disclosure encourages private investment in venture businesses and reduces reliance on public guarantees, supporting market-driven allocation of capital to innovative startups.
reforms.status_evidence: Disclosure by firms has been improved to encourage investment by individual investors in venture businesses.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted reform to improve venture capital market functioning through enhanced transparency. Supports the transition from public debt guarantees to market-based venture financing.
reforms.source_quote: Disclosure by firms has been improved to encourage investment by individual investors in venture businesses.

reforms.description: Japan launched the 'New Industry Development Strategy 2005' selecting seven priority areas for development, including four service sectors: business services, software contents, health/welfare, and environment/energy. The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) drew up detailed action plans for these priority areas.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directs public R&D and innovation support toward high-potential service sectors, aiming to accelerate productivity growth and economic dynamism in underperforming areas.
reforms.status_evidence: The strategy 'selected seven priority areas for development' and 'METI has drawn up detailed action plans for the priority areas.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant sectoral R&D initiative targeting underperforming service industries with structured action plans, but narrower in scope than economy-wide R&D system reform.
reforms.source_quote: The 'New Industry Development Strategy 2005' selected seven priority areas for development, including four service sectors; business services, software contents, health/welfare and environment/energy. The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) has drawn up detailed action plans for the priority areas.

reforms.description: In July 2006, METI announced a programme to develop the service industry as part of the 'New Strategy for Economic Growth', selecting six priority areas (health/welfare, childcare, tourism, business services, software contents, distribution/logistics) with a target to increase their market size by 70 trillion yen by 2015. The action plan 'Toward Innovation and Productivity Improvement in Service Industries' focuses on adopting scientific and engineering approaches, utilizing IT, building consumer credibility frameworks, improving quality assurance, developing human resources, facilitating entry, and expanding into foreign markets.
reforms.component_name: Toward Innovation and Productivity Improvement in Service Industries
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Combines sectoral R&D investment with human capital development and technology adoption to raise productivity and innovation capacity in service industries, directly supporting GDP per capita growth.
reforms.status_evidence: In July 2006, METI announced the programme with detailed action plan and specific targets for 2015.
reforms.importance_rationale: A comprehensive sectoral innovation initiative with explicit targets and multi-faceted action plan spanning R&D, human capital, and technology adoption across six service industries, representing significant but focused intervention.
reforms.source_quote: In July 2006, METI announced another programme to develop the service industry as part of a comprehensive initiative, entitled the 'New Strategy for Economic Growth'. This programme selected six priority areas for development; health/welfare, childcare, tourism, business services, software contents and distribution/logistics.

reforms.description: The Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) presented the 'Program for Enhancing Growth Potential' in 2007, aiming to boost productivity growth by 50% for all industries over five years. The action plan includes fostering human capital development, supporting job placement, raising SME competitiveness, pursuing service innovation through IT reform, and expanding the growth frontier by reforming the university system and promoting investment diversification.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Comprehensive productivity-focused programme combining human capital development, service sector innovation, and university system reform to raise economy-wide productivity and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The programme was 'presented by the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) in 2007' with explicit goals and action plan components.
reforms.importance_rationale: A major, economy-wide productivity enhancement programme with explicit 50% growth target over five years, spanning human capital, service innovation, university reform, and SME competitiveness. Represents structural ambition to reshape innovation and productivity across multiple sectors and institutions.
reforms.source_quote: The 'Program for Enhancing Growth Potential' presented by the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) in 2007. Its goal is to boost productivity growth, as measured by value-added per worker, by 50% for all industries over five years.

reforms.description: The 'SME Productivity Improvement Project' was included in 'Basic Policies 2007', aiming to enhance productivity of SMEs through IT utilization, corporate revitalization, and promotion of business start-ups. Major policy tools include providing financial support, R&D assistance, and developing human resources.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Provides direct R&D assistance and financial support to SMEs for innovation and productivity improvement, strengthening the innovation capacity of the private sector and supporting firm-level growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The project 'was included in Basic Policies 2007' with specified policy tools and objectives.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant SME-focused R&D and innovation support initiative combining financial assistance, R&D support, and human capital development, though narrower in scope than economy-wide programmes.
reforms.source_quote: The 'SME Productivity Improvement Project' was included in 'Basic Policies 2007'. This project aims at enhancing productivity of SMEs through IT utilisation, corporate revitalisation and the promotion of business start-ups. Major policy tools include providing financial support and R&D assistance and developing human resources.
